newsitem.title: USA: Schwarzenegger leaves hospital after heart surgery.
newsitem.headline: Schwarzenegger leaves hospital after heart surgery.

text.p: Action movie star Arnold Schwarzenegger, who underwent heart surgery last week to replace a heart valve, has been released from the hospital, his publicist said on Tuesday.
"Arnold's heart itself is strong and healthy," Dr. Vaughn Starnes, chief of Cardiothoracic Surgery at the University of Southern California University Hospital was quoted as saying in a statement.
Starnes, who led the team of three surgeons who operated on the Austrian-born actor last Wednesday to correct a congenital condition, said he was pleased with Schwarzenegger's recovery.

"He will resume his full active lifestyle with no limitations, restrictions or medications at all. I want to reassure his fans that he is stronger than ever and he'll be back at work this summer," Starnes's statement said.

Schwarzenegger, 49, who is married to television newscaster Maria Shriver, niece of the late President John Kennedy, chose to have the surgery to replace an aortic valve even though the condition had caused him no health problems.

In a statement, the actor and former "Mr Universe" bodybuilder said: "Chosing to undergo open heart surgery when I never felt sick was the hardest decision I've ever made. I can now look forward to a long and healthy life with my family."
Schwarzenegger thanked the staff at USC University Hospital -- the location of his surgery which had been kept a secret until his discharge.
Schwarzenegger is expected to rest until the end of May, when he will begin promoting the new movie "Batman and Robin" in which he plays the villain, Mr. Freeze.
